name: zhang-finite-example
authority: Research 0129 section 3; this contract authorizes one bounded run and nothing else
question: Can the finite-example criterion certify a plane-geometry identity by evaluation only, with no expansion of the conclusion, and where does its a priori degree bound come from?
level: External exact rational and directed-rounding evaluation over Q: every point of a declared grid, degree bounds propagated from the construction, a randomized check of the criterion itself, and falsified and sharpness controls
domain: Plane incidence statements already carried by this repository's Wu rounds: Pappus, Pascal for a parabola, a hyperbola and a circle, the Ceva conclusion with and without its hypothesis, and one deliberately mis-paired Pascal companion. Parameters are the free points of a parametrised configuration; the conclusion is a homogeneous 3x3 determinant of cross products of lines.

objects.criterion: A polynomial C in n free parameters with degree at most d_i in parameter i is identically zero if and only if it vanishes at every point of a grid with d_i + 1 distinct values in coordinate i, for every i. The forward implication is the certificate; the converse is what fixes the grid size.
objects.arithmetic_modes: One formula, three arithmetics: Fraction (the certificate), Decimal with directed rounding (a numerical pass with enclosures), and degree vectors only (the a priori bound).

statements.pappus: A, B, C on the x axis and a, b, c on the y axis, hexagon A, b, C, a, B, c; the three intersections of opposite sides are collinear. Six parameters.
statements.parabola_pascal: Six points (t, t^2, 1) in hexagon order; the three intersections of opposite sides are collinear. Six parameters.
statements.hyperbola_pascal: Six points represented by (t^2, 1, t), which is the affine point (t, 1/t) scaled by t; the same Pascal conclusion. Six parameters.
statements.circle_pascal: Six points (1 - t^2, 2t, 1 + t^2) on the unit circle; the same Pascal conclusion. Six parameters.
statements.ceva_conclusion: The Ceva collinearity conclusion as a polynomial in (t, e, f) with no hypothesis imposed. Three parameters, a priori bound 1 in each.
statements.ceva_chart: The Ceva hypothesis solved for f, substituted into the conclusion, with the chart denominator cleared. Two parameters, a priori bound 2 in each.
statements.wrong_pairing: The parabola Pascal conclusion with one side pairing exchanged; it is not an identity, so the criterion must fail on it and produce a witness.

objects.degree_bound: Propagated from the construction: multiplication adds degree vectors, addition takes their componentwise maximum, and constants have the zero vector. No expansion of the conclusion is performed to obtain any bound.
objects.grids: A declared integer grid with values 1..d_i+1 in coordinate i, and a declared random rational grid from a recorded seed with distinct nonzero values, filtered so that no two circle parameters are antipodal.

quantifiers: Every grid cell of every declared statement, evaluated in exact rational arithmetic, with the count and the number of nonzero values recorded
Every declared statement's a priori degree vector, its grid size, and its two independent grids
The interval pass over a declared subset of the rational grid, in Decimal with directed rounding at a declared precision
Degenerate parameter tuples, including coincident points and repeated parameters
The randomized criterion check and the sharpness witnesses
acceptance: The a priori degree vector of each statement is computed from the construction alone, and the grid size is the product of (d_i + 1)
Pappus, the parabola, the hyperbola and the circle Pascal identities vanish at every cell of both grids, so each is certified by the criterion without any expansion of the conclusion
The Ceva chart identity vanishes at every cell of both grids, so the hypothesis is handled by parametrising the hypothesis variety rather than by a symbolic remainder
The deliberately mis-paired Pascal is not certified: at least one grid cell is nonzero, and the first witness is reported with its exact value
The Ceva conclusion without its hypothesis is not certified, which shows that the hypothesis is required and that the criterion is not vacuous
The criterion itself is checked on random polynomials: one of degree at most d_i vanishing on the grid is the zero polynomial, and a nonzero one has a nonzero grid value
The grid size cannot be reduced: for every declared statement a nonzero polynomial of degree at most d_i vanishes on a grid one value short in that coordinate
The interval pass encloses zero at every sampled cell for the certified identities, and excludes zero at the reported witness of the mis-paired statement
The chart denominator of the Ceva parametrisation is the same polynomial as the non-degeneracy initial recorded by the Wu round, checked by the criterion itself with the recorded bound
Degenerate parameter tuples give exactly zero, and that is recorded as a statement about the polynomial and not about the geometry of a degenerate figure
Every certified identity is independently confirmed by exact symbolic expansion when the external library is present, and the library's absence is reported rather than assumed
protected: The Wu rounds 0181 and 0182 and the Feigenbaum rounds 0176 to 0180 are frozen and are not rewritten; their costs are read from their retained evidence and are not re-run here
This is external evidence: no native certificate, no geometry catalog admission, and the Pascal-rooted growth obligation stays Open
A grid certificate is a statement about one polynomial expression and its declared degree bound; it is not a proof about a degenerate geometric figure, and it is not a native Adva judgment

The criterion certifies identities, not statements with hypotheses: the Ceva hypothesis is handled by a parametrisation whose chart misses the locus where the denominator vanishes, and that locus is recorded
The published sources for the method are cited but are not re-derived: this run tests the criterion, not the source's own a priori bound theory
No metric, Arakelov, Monge-Ampere, mirror or Calabi-Yau content is introduced
residual: This certifies several plane incidence identities, and fails to certify two named non-identities, by evaluation at finitely many exact rational configurations with degree bounds propagated from the construction. It does not supply the theory that makes such bounds tight for a general statement class, it does not certify any statement whose hypothesis is not parametrised, and the parametrisation it does use covers only the chart where its denominator is nonzero.
